verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. No heading is missing and no PDF feature is lost; the only difference is markdown '#' depth, which is formatting, and it does not transcribe anything the PDF asserts. 1. NOTHING IS MISSING. All three headings are present in the transcription with the exact printed number and title: page-307.md line 7 '## 11.9.10.2 General format', line 21 '## 11.9.10.3 Syntax rule', line 26 '## 11.9.10.4 General rules' (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:13409, :13423, :13428). The kind label 'missing-heading' is simply wrong. Every rule under them is present too: the Syntax rule 1) literal-1 one-byte hexadecimal-alphanumeric, General rules 1)-7) including sub-items 5)a)-e) and the NOTE, all matching the rendered page. 2. THE PDF DOES NOT TYPOGRAPHICALLY DISTINGUISH THESE LEVELS. I rendered page 306 (dpi 300) specifically to compare parent against child, because page 307 alone cannot settle it. On page 306, '11.9.10 INITIALIZE clause' and '11.9.10.1 General' are printed in the SAME bold face, at the SAME point size, at the SAME left margin, with the SAME surrounding leading. '11.9.9.3 Syntax rules' higher on the same page is that identical style as well, and so are 11.9.10.2 / .3 / .4 on page 307. In this ISO PDF the third-level clause heading and its fourth-level subsection headings are typographically INDISTINGUISHABLE. Hierarchy in the printed standard is carried by the dotted clause NUMBER alone. Rendering both at '##' is therefore a faithful rendering of what is printed, not a loss of it -- there is no depth cue in the PDF for the markdown to have dropped. 3. THE HIERARCHY IS EXPLICITLY PRESERVED IN THE MARKDOWN, TWICE. The dotted number is verbatim in every heading text ('11.9.10.2'), and each heading carries its own generated anchor immediately above it: , , . Containment 11.9.10 -> 11.9.10.2 is recoverable losslessly from either. Meaning is unchanged; a tool that navigates by clause number (the only structure the PDF actually encodes) sees the correct tree. 4. THE CLAIM'S CONVENTION PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD DOC-WIDE. The claim rests on '###' being the established depth for four-component headings. Tallied over the whole transcription, four-component numbered headings appear 162 times at '##', 620 at '###', and 24 at '####'; three-component headings appear 276 times at '##', 508 at '###', 17 at '####'. There is no single convention on page 307 to violate. Decisively, the transcription already flattens exactly this relationship one level up and in the same neighbourhood: '## 11.9 OPTIONS paragraph' (:13142) and '## 11.9.7 ENTRY-CONVENTION clause' (:13258) are both at '##', so by the claim's own reasoning 11.9.7 is already 'a peer of' its parent 11.9. That is a pre-existing, pervasive trait of the transcription's flattening, not a page-307 content defect. 5. THE CLAIM ALSO MISDESCRIBES ITS OWN SCOPE. It presents the flattening as affecting the three subsections on page 307. In fact the whole 11.9.10 block is at '##' including '## 11.9.10.1 General' (:13396), and the immediately preceding '## 11.9.9.3 Syntax rules' (:13378) is flattened too -- both of which are printed on page 306, not 307. So even read charitably as a house-style normalization nit, the boundary drawn is wrong and the page attribution is wrong. Bottom line: the difference is markdown markup depth only, in a document with no consistent depth convention, transcribing a PDF that draws no typographic distinction at this boundary, with the hierarchy fully retained in both the heading text and the anchor ids. Rejected under 'the text is actually present' and 'the difference is only formatting'. Severity 'structural' is unsupported.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. All three headings (11.9.10.2 General format, 11.9.10.3 Syntax rule, 11.9.10.4 General rules) and all their rules are present and correct in the transcription; nothing is missing. The observation reduces to a cosmetic markdown heading-depth inconsistency: this block uses '##' where much of the document uses '###' for four-component clause numbers. It is not a PDF-vs-markdown divergence, because the ISO PDF prints 11.9.10 and 11.9.10.1/.2/.3/.4 in identical bold face, size and margin (verified on the 300-dpi renders of pages 306 and 307) -- the printed standard encodes this hierarchy only through the dotted clause number, which the markdown reproduces verbatim and additionally mirrors in per-heading anchors (section-11-9-10-2 etc.), so containment is not lost. The transcription has no doc-wide depth convention to violate (four-component headings: 162 at '##', 620 at '###', 24 at '####'), and it already flattens the same parent/child relationship at '## 11.9' vs '## 11.9.7'. If normalized as house style, the fix must cover '## 11.9.10.1 General' and '## 11.9.9.3 Syntax rules' as well -- both printed on page 306, not 307 -- so the finding is also mis-scoped and mis-paginated. Cosmetic at most; not structural.
